messages:
anya: Quick follow-up from the RFC yesterday — I'm proposing we strip the old monolithic 'adapter' layer and replace it with sandboxed, per-tenant adapters that run as isolated processes. Reason: ownership ambiguity today and the adapter is a big source of accidental coupling. Thoughts?

mike: Sounds promising. Main concern is startup/cold-start for low-traffic tenants. How do we avoid latency regressions on single-request bursts? :thinking:

anya: Good call. Two mitigations: 1) keep a tiny in-process shim that proxies hot tenants for 6 months, 2) allow adapter processes to be kept warm via a lightweight pinger / lease. We can also pack multiple tiny tenants into a single process to amortize startup.

sanjay: For the shim, do you mean we keep the current adapter API surface in the runtime but implement it as a proxy to the sandbox when available? Any example contract?

anya: Exactly. Rough sketch:
```
POST /v1/adapter/execute
{ tenant_id: "t123", payload: {...} }
// runtime checks local registry -> if sandbox live forward, else run internal shim fallback
```
The shim must be minimal: no model logic, just routing + basic auth.

lena: How about data isolation and KMS keys per-tenant? Sandboxed processes sound better for keys, but we should outline the KMS flow. If a process crashes we must ensure keys aren't leaked in core memory.

mike: Also need to think about telemetry. Right now adapter logs are mixed with runtime. We should emit structured span with adapter_id and tenant tags so we can track tail latency by tenant.

anya: Agreed on telemetry. Plan: add a mandatory trace/span tag adapter.instance and adapter.mode (shim|sandbox|fallback). We'll also emit a tiny heartbeat metric for process liveness.

sanjay: Migration strategy idea: wave 0 = internal tenants only (infra, test), wave 1 = low-QPS customers, wave 2 = sensitive customers with dedicated KMS. Each wave has a compatibility gate: contract tests passing + latency delta < 5% for 72h.

mike: Can we automate contract tests in CI? I can add a harness that runs the runtime shim against a fake sandbox and verifies wire-level compatibility. That will be a blocker before we flip any production traffic.

lena: Security ops ask: enforce ephemeral credentials for adapters and rotate leases every 24h. Also add runtime guardrails to kill processes that exceed memory or CPU budgets.

anya: Sounds right. Operational playbook:
- create sandbox runtime image (non-root, seccomp profile)
- add lease/heartbeat + metrics
- add contract-test harness to CI
- rollout in waves with telemetry gates
- maintain shim for 6 months, then remove after all waves complete

mike: Timeline suggestion: prototype in 2 sprints, infra + security hardening sprint, then gradual rollout over next quarter. I'll take prototype.

sanjay: I'll own telemetry + contract tests. Lena, can you own seccomp + KMS flow?

lena: Yup. I'll open the KMS design doc and a short checklist for process hardening.

anya: I'll open the RFC follow-up PR with the migration plan and the exact shim API. Also adding these owners to the RFC thread.

deploy-bot: Created issue INFRA-4892: "sandboxed adapters: prototype + migration plan" assigned to mike, sanjay, lena. Link: https://redwood.example/INFRA-4892 :zap:

mike: One more runtime detail — prefer we expose a single health endpoint that returns adapter.ready=true only when contract tests have succeeded for that tenant to avoid premature traffic.

anya: Good idea. We'll add a readiness mode: ready=false until smoke + contract checks pass.

lena: We should also add a small compatibility header so old clients can detect shim vs sandbox: X-Adapter-Mode: shim|sandbox|fallback. That helps debugging.

sanjay: Agree. Okay team — looks like we have a clear path. I'll start the contract harness PR and drop links here when ready.

anya: Thanks all. If no objections by EOD I'll file the formal RFC amendment and kick off the prototype ticket. :thumbsup:
